**What this PR does / why we need it**:

This PR fixed a wrong indentation level in "kubectl describe node" output. This is the current output.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/60682957/96225284-d4543c00-0fcb-11eb-98b2-4afb5707a373.png)

Items in "Capacity", "Allocatable" and "System Info" have only 1 spaces at the head. Originally they were declared as `LEVEL_0` with 2 spaces, but for some reasons it outputs with only 1 space.

Because any other parts are using "2-spaces" indentation level, for consistency, it should be fixed.
This PR changes them to use `LEVEL_1` to keep the indentation 2 spaces.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

issue_context.title: Invalid indentation level in kubectl describe node output
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:

When executing "kubectl describe node", indentation level of items in "Capacity", "Allocatable" and "System Info" is not consistent with others. Although other parts have 2 spaces, they only have one space.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/60682957/96226149-29448200-0fcd-11eb-8790-69c70e7b09d4.png)

**What you expected to happen**:

Indentation with 2 spaces.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

Run "kubectl describe node" for an arbitrary cluster.

**Anything else we need to know?**:

N/A

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): v1.19.2. Additionally, kubectl version is v1.16.3 but I don't think it's fixed in the latest one.
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: minikube
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): macOS
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): Darwin PC2350 19.6.0 Darwin Kernel Version 19.6.0: Mon Aug 31 22:12:52 PDT 2020; root:xnu-6153.141.2~1/RELEASE_X86_64 x86_64
- Install tools: Docker
